# Bootstrap reference systems

`BootstrapSO5.m` is the exact three-equation SO(5) vector result captured before
the performance changes. `BootstrapSp2.m` likewise preserves the exact
Sp(2) system, including the automatically registered pseudoreal dual. `BootstrapG2Mixed.m` is the exact nine-equation G2
vector-plus-singlet system, independently checked through full tensor crossing
reconstruction by `BootstrapChecks.m`.

The tests compare coefficient row spaces rather than textual output. This
allows equation reordering and different row bases. The numerical check uses
50-digit arithmetic with an error threshold of 1e-25, including irrational
coefficients such as 1/Sqrt[7].

## Independent Lie-algebra reference

`LieGAP.m` is generated by `python3 test/reference/generate-gap.py` using GAP
4.11.1, without loading any autoboot code. Its 15 cases cover A2/A3/A4,
B2/B3/B5, C4/C5, D5/D6, E6/E7/E8, F4 and G2. Each record stores the Cartan matrix,
dimension, dominant weights with multiplicities, and tensor decomposition
with multiplicities. The generator applies the explicit F4 node permutation `[2,4,3,1]`
between GAP and Bourbaki; GAP's Cartan convention is the transpose of ours.
The Cartan matrices are checked before comparing weight labels.

GAP and the optimized autoboot decomposition both use Klimyk's formula,
with separate implementations. The older character convolution / highest-weight
subtraction algorithm remains as an additional A3/E6/G2 cross-check.
See the [GAP Lie-algebra reference, section 64.13](https://gap-system.github.io/gap/doc/ref/chap64.html).
Fixtures can be consumed by `make test` without GAP Lie packages or a network
connection. Regeneration needs only GAP core and Python 3.


`BootstrapF4.m` preserves the five-equation exact F4 defining-26 system after
full CG isometry/completeness, Lie intertwining, and all-component four-tensor
crossing checks. `benchmark/ValidateLarge.wls` compares it in both arithmetic
modes. It is an autoboot regression fixture, not an external mathematical oracle.
